sanskrit: indre lokā indre tapa indre 'dhy ṛtam āhitam | indraṃ tvā vidma pratyakṣaṃ skambhe sarvaṃ samāhitam ||
english: In Indra are the worlds, in Indra is heat, in Indra is cosmic order established. We know you as Indra directly — in the Skambha all is gathered together.

sanskrit: nāma nāmnā johavīmi purā sūryāt puroṣasaḥ | yad adaḥ prathamaṃ saṃbabhūva saha tat svarājyaṃ jagāma yasmān na param asti bhūtam ||
english: I call out name by name, before the sun, before the dawn. That which first came into being — together with it, sovereignty departed; beyond that there is no being whatsoever.

sanskrit: yasya bhūmiḥ pramāntarikṣam utodaram | divaṃ yaś cakre mūrdhānaṃ tasmai jyeṣṭhāya brahmaṇe namaḥ ||
english: He whose measure is the earth, whose belly is the atmosphere — who made heaven his head — to that greatest Brahman, homage.

sanskrit: yasya sūryaś cakṣuś candramāś ca punar navaḥ | agniṃ yaś cakra āsyaṃ tasmai jyeṣṭhāya brahmaṇe namaḥ ||
english: He whose eye is the sun and whose moon is ever renewed — who made fire his mouth — to that greatest Brahman, homage.

sanskrit: yasya vātaḥ prāṇāpānau cakṣur aṅgiraso 'bhuvan | diśo yaś cakre prajñānīs tasmai jyeṣṭhāya brahmaṇe namaḥ ||
english: He whose in-breath and out-breath is the wind, whose eyes became the Aṅgirases — who made the directions his cognizing faculty — to that greatest Brahman, homage.

sanskrit: yaḥ śramāt tapaso jāto lokān sarvān samānaśe | somaṃ yaś cakre kevalaṃ tasmai jyeṣṭhāya brahmaṇe namaḥ ||
english: He who was born from toil and austerity and pervaded all the worlds — who made Soma his alone — to that greatest Brahman, homage.

sanskrit: skambho dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dyām utāmūṃ skambho dādhārorv antarikṣam | skambho dādhāra pradiśaḥ ṣaḍ urvīḥ skambha idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanam ā viveśa ||
english: The Skambha upheld the earth and yonder heaven; the Skambha upheld the vast atmosphere. The Skambha upheld the six broad directions; the Skambha entered into this entire world of beings.

sanskrit: kathaṃ vāto nelayati kathaṃ na ramate manaḥ | kim āpaḥ satyaṃ prepsantīḥ pra caṅkramīti sarvadā ||
english: Why does the wind never cease? Why does the mind not rest? Why do the waters, ever seeking truth, keep moving on forever?

sanskrit: mahad yakṣaṃ bhuvanasya madhye tapasi krāntaṃ salilasya pṛṣṭhe | tasmiṃ chrayante ya u ke ca devā vṛkṣasya skambhaṃ parita iva śākhāḥ ||
english: A great Yakṣa in the midst of the world, suffused with austerity upon the surface of the waters — upon it all the gods whatsoever take their refuge, like branches around the trunk of a tree.

sanskrit: yasmai hastābhyāṃ pādābhyāṃ vācā śrotreṇa cakṣuṣā | yasmai devā sadā baliṃ prayacchanti vimite 'mitaṃ skambhaṃ taṃ brūhi katamaḥ svid eva saḥ ||
english: He to whom with both hands and both feet, with voice, with hearing, with sight — to whom the gods ever offer tribute, the bounded to the boundless — tell me of that Skambha: who indeed is he?

sanskrit: apa tasya tamo hataṃ vyāvṛttaḥ sa pāpmanā | sarvāṇi tasmin jyotīṃṣi yāni trīṇi prajāpatau ||
english: From him darkness has been struck away; he has turned back from evil. All three lights that exist in Prajāpati — all are in him.

sanskrit: yo vetasaṃ hiraṇyayaṃ tiṣṭhantaṃ salile veda | sa vai guhyaḥ prajāpatiḥ ||
english: He who knows the golden reed standing in the waters — that one is truly the hidden Prajāpati.

sanskrit: na prajāpatim aty eti nāty eti parameṣṭhinam | utota tatra no vṛta yaj jyeṣṭhaṃ paro atyayat ||
english: No one surpasses Prajāpati, no one surpasses Parameṣṭhin. And yet there too our attention was turned, where the eldest passed beyond the beyond.

sanskrit: asti vai tat paro bhūmer asti vai tat paro divaḥ | lokā vai tasmin saṃprotā yasminn otāḥ prajā imāḥ ||
english: That truly exists beyond the earth; that truly exists beyond the sky. The worlds are strung upon it, and upon it these creatures are woven.

sanskrit: antaḥpātre rerihati dūrśe durnihitaiṣiṇi | uruṇḍe abhicaṅkrame vakmake bastavāsini sarvāsāṃ bhaṇvā vaḥ sākaṃ nāmadheyāni vidmasi | yati jātāni vas tati naśyatetaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: You who lick inside the pot, O ill-looking seeker of misplaced things — O Uruṇḍa, O Abhicaṅkrama, O Vakmaka, O Bastavāsini — we know all your names together, O she-demons. As many as are born among you, so many shall perish from here, O Sadānvāḥ.

sanskrit: karṇā dṛṣadrathāmaham urukīṃ keśinīṃ krakum | khaḍurīm ambarīṣyaṃ nāśayāmaḥ sadānvāḥ || prapāṭhaka ||
english: Karṇa, Dṛṣadrathāmahā, Urukī, Keśinī, Kraku, Khaḍurī, Ambarīṣyā — we destroy these Sadānvāḥ she-demons.

sanskrit: paṇḍugirāṃ phāladatīm asaṃsūktanigāriṇīm | asātāḥ sarvā vo brūmo naśyatetaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: Paṇḍugirā, Phāladatī, she who swallows without proper incantation — all of you we declare harmful; perish from here, O Sadānvāḥ.

sanskrit: yāḥ śayānaṃ jambhayanti naktam icchanty āturam | atho janasya suptasya mukhā hastāt pra rihanti datsu datkavanocitās tā ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Those she-demons who devour one who is lying down, who seek by night the sick man, and who lick from the mouth and hand of a sleeping person — accustomed to gnawing with their teeth — those we drive away from here.

sanskrit: āpatantīr vikṣiṇānā vastagandhāḥ sadānvāḥ | bhaṇvā (a)sinā totsyāmi tīkṣṇaśṛṅga ivarṣabhaḥ ||
english: The Sadānvāḥ she-demons who come flying and scattering, smelling of goat — I will pierce them with the Bhaṇvā sword, as a bull with sharp horns.

sanskrit: sadānvāḥ sādānveyāṃ strīpuṃsām̐ ubhayān saha | sahe sahasvān sahasā vi mṛdho hanmi rakṣasaḥ ||
english: O Sadānvāḥ, O progeny of Sādānvī — both women and men together. With strength, powerfully, with might, I crush and smite the Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: caturdaṃṣṭrān kumbhamuṣkān dīrghakeśām̐ asṛnmukhān | alābugandhīn undurān durṇāmno nāśayāmasi ||
english: The four-fanged ones, the jar-testicled ones, the long-haired ones, the blood-faced ones, those smelling of bottle-gourd, the rats — ill-named ones, we destroy you.

sanskrit: stambe jātā adhi bāle rodākām̐ rudatīṃ tvat | durṇāmnīḥ sarvāḥ santokā nāśayāmaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: Born in the thicket, upon the tender one who weeps and wails from you — all of you ill-named ones together with your offspring, we destroy, O Sadānvāḥ.

sanskrit: yāsāṃ jātāni krośanti bhitsv antar vane jvala upa vṛkṣeṣu śerate | (…) ||
english: Those whose offspring cry out within the clefts, and who blaze in the forest, who lie down upon the trees — [the remainder of the verse is lost in the manuscript].

sanskrit: yā vātābhra utpatite carttā varṣeṇa vidyutā śālā icchanti satvaram | durṇāmnīḥ sarvāḥ santokā nāśayāmaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: Those who roam when storm-clouds rise, along with rain and lightning, who quickly seek out dwellings — all of you ill-named ones together with your offspring, we destroy, O Sadānvāḥ.
